description: This course will cover the research methods, theoretical principles and research findings on the growth and change that occurs from infancy to childhood across multiple domains of development (e.g., physical, cognitive, social, emotional), focusing on the interplay of individual abilities and characteristics, sociocultural experiences, and their bidirectional influence on children's developmental outcomes. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Recommended: H_D_FS 8210

subject: H_D_FS
title: Early Childhood Education and Care: History, Child Development, and Equity
description: Overview of the research on young children (birth through age eight), demographics of this population, critical domains of development, significance of early brain development, and issues of inequality and disproportionality that deeply shape child outcomes. Students will identify the critical need to develop ECEC policies grounded in research and practice, and the effectiveness and limitations of ECEC policies to address fundamental issues of inequality. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Recommended: It is recommended that this course is the first one taken in the Early Childhood and Family Policy graduate certificate program

subject: H_D_FS
title: Cognitive Development
description: (same as PSYCH 8420 ). Study of the development of reasoning, perception and language. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: H_D_FS
title: Social and Emotional Development
description: (same as PSYCH 8440 ). Seminar on emotional and social development in children, with focus on research and theory on the impact of various family, school, and societal factors. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: H_D_FS
title: Adolescence and Emerging Adulthood
description: Seminar on development during adolescence and emerging adulthood from biological, cognitive, psychsocial, and cultural perspectives, and with a focus on health-related attitudes and behaviors. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: H_D_FS
title: Parenting Education
description: Study of theories, models, research and skills regarding parenting effectiveness and parent-child relations in the context of Western and Eastern cultures.  Included are comparisons of the relative strengths and weaknesses of various parenting approaches, historical perspective on parenthood and children, parenting roles, strategies for contemporary parenting, developmental interaction from infancy through adulthood and selected special concerns of parents.  A Bio-Ecological Systems approach will be utilized in this course.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: H_D_FS
title: Lifespan Development
description: This course covers the human development including the cognitive, social-emotional, motor, language, and moral domains from both a lifespan and a bio-ecological perspective.  Course content focuses on the major theories of development as well as current research on the micro-macro interrelationship.  Students who complete this course will have a better understanding of individual human developmental processes and their relationship with context and within family and community matters.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: H_D_FS
title: Remarriage & Stepfamilies: Development, Dynamics, & Intervention
description: The processes of remarriage and reconstituted family dynamics; special developmental needs and intervention models will be studied. The impact on children is considered. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: instructor's consent

subject: H_D_FS
title: Family Interaction
description: Examination of intrafamilial interaction.  Includes an overview of theories used to study family interaction, critical review of the assessment of family interaction; and examination of contemporary research on family interaction focusing on intra and inter-generational relationships. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: H_D_FS
title: Children, Families and Public Policy
description: Seminar on societal issues relating to children and families, with focus on the development of public policies. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: H_D_FS
title: Early Childhood Education and Care Today: Examining Practices, Policies, and Key Issues
description: This course focuses on the practice of Early Childhood Education and Care, as well as the role of families and policymakers in altering practices and policies. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Recommended: It is recommended to take H_D_FS 8415 History, Child Development, and Equity before this course

subject: H_D_FS
title: Poverty
description: Implications of poverty for child, adult, and family functioning.  Poverty-related policies and programs. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: H_D_FS
title: Readings in Human Development and Family Science
description: Readings in recent research; critical evaluation.  Prerequisites: instructor's consent

subject: H_D_FS
title: Internship in Human Development and Family Science
description: Internships and/or field training experiences under supervision.  Graded on S/U basis only.  Prerequisites: instructor's consent

subject: H_D_FS
title: Research in Human Development and Family Science
description: Independent research leading to thesis or dissertation. Graded on S/U basis only.

subject: H_D_FS
title: Teaching Practicum
description: Supervised experience in teaching various audiences, including college students, professionals, and community residents. Graded on S/U basis only.  Prerequisites: instructor's consent

subject: H_D_FS
title: Advanced Research Methods in Human Development and Family Science
description: This course offers an advanced examination of research issues in Human Development and Family Science (HDFS). It is designed to strengthen students' skills as both producers and critical consumers of research. Students will engage in advanced methodological training, including the selection of appropriate measurement strategies, research designs, and analytic approaches commonly used in HDFS research. Particular emphasis will be placed on aligning research questions, study design, and analytic methods. Key topics covered in the course include aligning theory and research, conceptual frameworks and methodological decision-making, psychometric properties and measurement invariance, advanced multivariate statistical techniques, multicollinearity, sample size and power analysis considerations, and effective management of missing data. In addition, students will develop skills in critically reviewing empirical research and understanding essential considerations related to the dissemination and publication of research findings. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: H_D_FS 8200 or instructor's consent required Recommended: It is strongly recommended that students will have taken some statistics/research methods courses, have a solid understanding of inferential and univariate statistics, and have had some exposure to multivariate analysis

subject: H_D_FS
title: Research Practicum in Human Development and Family Science
description: Independent research activities in conjunction with faculty. Graded on S/U basis only.  Prerequisites: instructor's consent

subject: H_D_FS
title: Application of Advanced Statistics in Human Development and Family Science
description: This course will provide an in-depth examination of some of the advanced statistical methods and analysis common in the field human development and family science (HDFS), including common approaches to modeling longitudinal and dyadic/group level data. Students will gain practical experience (a) using publicly available datasets, (b) conducting a variety of analyses specific to the study of development and family/group level data, (c) interpreting results, and (d) writing results. Students will learn about data and data structure required for advanced analyses. Credit Hour s : 3 Recommended: ESC_PS 9660 and ESC_PS 9710

subject: H_D_FS
title: Qualitative Methods
description: Examines the following selected qualitative research approaches appropriate for the study of nursing phenomena and the extension or modification of scientific knowledge so as to be relevant to nursing: case study research methods, verbal qualitative approaches, and nonverbal qualitative approaches. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Introduction to Industrial Engineering
description: Introduction to industrial engineering profession, the Industrial and Systems Engineering department, and the core topics of industrial engineering. Introduction to problem solving, ethics and industrial engineering design and analysis techniques. Graded on A-F basis only.

subject: ISE
title: Fundamentals of Systems Design and Analysis
description: An introduction to a systems engineering approach for designing, integrating, and managing complex systems (financial, healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, service, etc.) over their lifecycle. This includes system modeling, specification, structured problem solving, system design methodology, and the application of artificial intelligence to address the trade-offs between system performance, lifecycle cost, and operability/reliability. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: MATH 1500

subject: ISE
title: Probability and Statistics for Engineers
description: Introduction to data analysis, probability concepts, random variables, parameter estimation and hypothesis testing. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: MATH 1500 . Restricted to Engineering Students who are non-IMSE majors

subject: ISE
title: Linear Algebra for Engineers
description: Study of linear algebra methods used in engineering analysis, modeling, and system optimization. Topics include solutions of linear systems, vector spaces, least squares and orthogonality, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and matrix factorizations with applications to networks, dynamic systems, and optimization problems. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: MATH 1700

subject: ISE
title: Engineering Economic Decision-Making
description: Fundamentals of economic decision-making from an engineering perspective. Includes conceptual basis of economic analysis (interest, inflation), principles for decision making (cost/benefits, breakeven analysis, risk and uncertainty, multi-objectives/attributes), generation of engineering economic parameters (life-cycle analysis), and the application of economic decision making in different context (governmental policy, time-phased, and scarce capital). Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: sophomore standing

subject: ISE
title: Topics in Industrial and Systems Engineering
description: Current and new technical developments in industrial engineering. May be repeated to 6 hours.  Prerequisites: instructor's consent

subject: ISE
title: Manufacturing and Supply Systems
description: Provide a structured approach for the design and optimization of a system throughout its lifecycle: techniques following the logical sequence of strategic analysis, system design, implementation, and monitoring. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 2030

subject: ISE
title: Probability Models for Engineers
description: Introduction to probability concept and theory, random variables, discrete and continuous probability distributions, joint probability distributions. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Grade of C- or better in MATH 1500

subject: ISE
title: Probability Models for Engineers - Honors
description: Introduction to probability concept and theory, random variables, discrete and continuous probability distributions, joint probability distributions.   Honors eligibility required Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in MATH 1500

subject: ISE
title: Introduction to Manufacturing Methods
description: (same as MAE 3500 ). This course is an introduction to the engineering principles of manufacturing processes, ranging from traditional to state-of-the-art. The course will emphasize material processing, selection, and design considerations for manufacturing. The course introduces critical aspects of manufacturing process engineering through a combination of lectures, videos, class discussions, and case studies to engage students. By the end of the course, students are expected to learn the fundamentals of manufacturing and manufacturing processes. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 2 Prerequisites or Corequisites: ENGINR 2200 Prerequisites: MAE 1100

subject: ISE
title: Computer Aided Design and Manufacturing Processes Laboratory
description: This course covers the product realization process from design, process planning, to manufacturing, including CE, DFA/DFM, CAD, CAPP, CAM, CNC. The course uses active learning with hands-on laboratory projects, videos, and class discussions.  By the end of the course, students will learn the fundamentals of manufacturing and manufacturing processes, and the product realization process from CAD to CAM, primarily through concept learning and hands-on laboratory exercises.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 2 Prerequisites: MAE 1100 ; Junior standing; restricted to IMSE students Corequisites: ISE 3500 or MAE 3500

subject: ISE
title: Industrial Robotics
description: An experiential industrial robotics course that will take students from fundamentals to intermediate programming of multiple industrial robotic systems. Students will learn with both six-axis articulated arm robots and state-of-the-art collaborative robots. Additionally, students will explore conceptual and applied machine vision concepts utilizing industrial machine vision systems. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: PHYSCS 2760

subject: ISE
title: Ergonomics and Workstation Design
description: Ergonomics and human factors theories applied to the design of man-machine systems.  Discussion of ergonomic methods for measurement, assessment, and evaluation, with major topics including workstation design, environmental stresses, and workplace safety.  Includes lab. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE students. ENGINR 1200 and ISE 4110

subject: ISE
title: Ergonomics and Workstation Design - Writing Intensive
description: Ergonomics and human factors theories applied to the design of man-machine systems.  Discussion of ergonomic methods for measurement, assessment, and evaluation, with major topics including workstation design, environmental stresses, and workplace safety.  Includes lab.  Prerequisites: Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE students. ENGINR 1200 and ISE 4110

subject: ISE
title: Topics in Industrial and Systems Engineering
description: Current and new technical developments in industrial engineering. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Problems in Industrial Engineering
description: Supervised investigation in industrial engineering presented in form of an engineering report.

subject: ISE
title: Engineering Statistics
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7110 ). Understanding and application of statistical analysis techniques. Emphasis on hypothesis testing, regression analysis, analysis of variance (ANOVA) and design of experiments (DOE). Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE students or by Departmental consent. Grade of C- or better in ISE 3110

subject: ISE
title: Deterministic Models in Operations Research
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7210 ). Study of linear, network, and integer optimization models for deterministic decision-making with emphasis on model development, interpretation, and applications in engineering and management systems. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Grade of C- or better in ISE 2210

subject: ISE
title: Optimization Modeling and Computational Methods
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7220 ). Modeling and solution techniques for mathematical optimization, including linear, nonlinear, integer, and stochastic programming. Emphasis on formulation of models for most-efficient use of solution algorithms.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 3110 , ISE 4210

subject: ISE
title: Stochastic Models in Operations Research
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7230 ). Introduces stochastic models and probabilistic optimization for decision-making under uncertainty, emphasizing model formulation, performance analysis, and applications in engineering and management systems. Topics include dynamic programming, Markov chains, Poisson processes, queueing theory, and inventory theory. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Grade of C- or better in ISE 2210 and ISE 3110 , or Departmental consent required

subject: ISE
title: Discrete-Event Simulation for Digital Twin Applications
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7280 ). Introduces principles and methods for modeling and analyzing discrete-event stochastic systems. Lecture topics include queuing theory, Monte Carlo simulation, random number and variate generation, input and output analysis, variance reduction, and simulation-based experiment design. The laboratory component emphasizes developing virtual 3D simulation models using advanced software platforms to represent, analyze, and improve system performance in support of digital twin applications across manufacturing, logistics, and service operations. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Grade of C- or better in ISE 4110

subject: ISE
title: Integrated Production Systems Design
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7310 ). Design and operation of production systems, including lean six sigma concepts, just-in-time/kanban, facility layout and material flow issues. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE students or by Departmental consent. ISE 2030 , ISE 2710 , ISE 4210 , ISE 4280

subject: ISE
title: Material Flow and Logistics System Design
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7330 ). Modeling and analysis of structural and operational issues associated with material-flow system design including facility location, warehouse/inventory systems, and distribution/transportation systems. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 4210 and ISE 4280

subject: ISE
title: AI-Driven Production and Operations Analytics
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7350 ). This course covers quantitative methods for forecasting, scheduling, and production control in manufacturing and service systems, enhanced with generative AI tools. Students will leverage generative AI to develop, code, and analyze simulation and optimization models using Python. The focus is on practical applications of AI-assisted modeling to improve operational decision-making and system performance in real-world production and service environments. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 4210 and ISE 4230 . Departmental consent required for non-ISE majors

subject: ISE
title: Supply Chain Engineering
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7360 ). Modeling and analysis of supply chain network design and management issues including integration of production, inventory control, supplier selection, risk management and logistics network design. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 4350

subject: ISE
title: Service Systems Engineering and Management
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7370 ). Service systems contribute to more than 75% of US GDP and provide close to 80% employment. This course introduces students to service system engineering and management and will discuss models, concepts and solution methods important in the design, control, and operation of service systems. In addition, this course will provide students the ability to apply industrial engineering and operations research tools for analyzing service enterprises, including supply chain engineering, financial engineering and revenue management. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 4210 or instructor's consent

subject: ISE
title: Six Sigma Methodology
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7380 ). An overview of the Six Sigma DMAIC methodology for analyzing and improving processes. Requires completing a Six Sigma Green Belt project. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in ISE 2110 or ISE 4110 or STAT 4710

subject: ISE
title: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt Project
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7385 ). Application of the Lean Six Sigma methodology in an industry-based project.  Prerequisites: ISE 4310

subject: ISE
title: Data Analytics and Machine Learning for Operations Intelligence
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7410 ). Introduces data analytics and machine learning methods for improving operational intelligence in organizational and industrial systems. Covers descriptive analytics models, including data visualization, dashboards, and statistical summaries, and machine learning pipelines that involve model development, evaluation, and interpretation. Topics include exploratory data analysis, descriptive statistics, supervised learning algorithms, and unsupervised machine learning. Emphasizes data preparation, model development, and model interpretation using R and Excel to build end-to-end machine learning pipelines and derive actionable insights for data-driven decision-making in manufacturing, supply chain, logistics, healthcare, and service operations. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: INFOTC 4401 or CMP_SC 1050 , and ISE 4110

subject: ISE
title: Web-Based Information Systems
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7420 ). Data models, design of databases using E-R, UML (Access/Oracle), web databases, web servers and interfaces (Visual Basic, JavaScript), E-commerce infrastructure (PDM, STEP, XML), data mining for management information and services. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 4410 and instructor's consent

subject: ISE
title: Introduction to Manufacturing Processes
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7500 ).  An introduction to the engineering principles of manufacturing processes, ranging from traditional (casting, forming, cutting, welding) to the state-of-the-art (additive). The course will emphasize material selection, process analysis and selection, and product design considerations for manufacturing. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites or Corequisites: ENGINR 2200 or MAE 2200 Prerequisites: MAE 1100

subject: ISE
title: Computer Aided Design and Manufacturing
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7550 ).  Product realization process from design, process planning, to manufacturing. Includes CE, DFS/DFM, CAD, CAPP, CNC, and survey of manufacturing methods. Credit Hour s : 4 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE students; Junior Standing Corequisites: ENGINR 2200

subject: ISE
title: Introduction to Rapid Prototyping
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7560 ). Course covers all five MU systems: FDM, SLS, SLA, Polyjet, 3DP.  Students will learn fundamental rapid prototyping and related concepts, and design and produce models from each system.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 4550

subject: ISE
title: Smart Manufacturing Systems
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7565 ). A lab-based introduction to smart manufacturing systems design and operation with respect to Industry 4.0. Course topics include: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), cyber-physical systems (CPS), artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins (DT), industrial automation and robotics, and cybersecurity in smart manufacturing. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Junior standing

subject: ISE
title: Industrial Automation and Control
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7570 ). Examination of industrial automation that covers the fundamental concepts of automation using industrial sensors, transducers, and instrumentation - to system integration with PLCs (programmable logic controllers) utilizing state-of-the-art programming software. The course utilizes experiential learning with hands-on laboratory projects to explore concepts in industrial automation and control.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: PHYSCS 2760

subject: ISE
title: Industrial Energy Efficiency and Management
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7580 ). Introduction to the fundamentals of industrial energy efficiency and management. Covers the essential concepts, best practices, management systems and current standards to achieve and improve energy efficiency in industrial settings, and utilizes hands-on experiences involving real assessment and analysis of industrial site visits and projects. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 2030 or instructor's consent

subject: ISE
title: Quality Engineering and Analytics
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7610 ).  Introduces concepts, theory, and analytical methodologies for quality planning, improvement, and control in manufacturing and service systems. Topics covered include process quality modeling, hypothesis testing, control charts, capability analysis, data visualization, text analytics. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE students or by Departmental consent. ISE 4110 . INFOTC 4401

subject: ISE
title: Introduction to Sales Engineering
description: Introduces the sales engineering profession. Overview of sales engineering in the different engineering disciplines. An introduction to problem-solving and sales engineering processes is covered. Various forms of technical and social communication are emphasized throughout the course. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Junior standing required

subject: ISE
title: Introduction to Life Cycle Analysis
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7720 ). Introduction to life cycle thinking, application of ISO standards for conducting an LCA. Students learn process, input-output and hybrid LCA modeling basics, in addition to the application of LCA skills and thinking to improve the performance of systems and processes. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Junior standing

subject: ISE
title: Entrepreneurial Innovation Management: Enterprise Conception
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7750 ). Develop a new business and technology plan including marketing, finance, engineering, manufacturing, and production concepts in this joint College of Engineering and College of Business course. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: sophomore standing

subject: ISE
title: Entrepreneurial Innovation Management: Enterprise Conception-Honors
description: Develop a new business and technology plan including marketing, finance, engineering, manufacturing, and production concepts in this joint College of Engineering and College of Business course. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: sophomore standing. Honors eligibility required

subject: ISE
title: Cognitive Ergonomics
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 7810 ). This course will cover the study of empirical research in Cognitive ergonomics and Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). Students will learn cognitive information processing, mental workload, human reliability, and empirical methods in HCI research. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Recommended: Junior or senior level undergraduate students

subject: ISE
title: Industrial Engineering Internship
description: An industry-based learning experience that provides opportunities to apply industrial engineering skills, concepts and theories in a practical context. Requires submission of an internship plan for prior approval and a final oral presentation / written report at the completion of the internship. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: instructor and departmental consent Recommended: junior standing

subject: ISE
title: Industrial Engineering COOP
description: An industry-based learning experience that provides opportunities to apply industrial engineering skills, concepts and theories in a practical context. Requires submission of a COOP plan for prior approval and a final oral presentation / written report at the completion of the COOP. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: instructor and departmental consent Recommended: junior standing

subject: ISE
title: Capstone Design I
description: Overview of professional engineering issues such as ethics, team dynamics, communication, and project management.  Includes team-based industrial assessments to develop skills in problem/opportunity identification.  Graded on A-F basis only.  Prerequisites or Corequisites: ISE 4310 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE students; Senior Standing

subject: ISE
title: Capstone Design I - Writing Intensive
description: Overview of professional engineering issues such as ethics, team dynamics, communication, and project management.  Includes team-based industrial assessments to develop skills in problem/opportunity identification.  Graded on A-F basis only.  Prerequisites or Corequisites: ISE 4310 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE students; Senior Standing

subject: ISE
title: Capstone Design II
description: Industry-based team design experience structured to integrate material presented throughout the Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering curriculum.  Must immediately follow ISE 4970 . Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE student; ISE 3810 , ISE 4310 , and ISE 4970

subject: ISE
title: Capstone Design II - Writing Intensive
description: Industry-based team design experience structured to integrate material presented throughout the Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering curriculum.  Must immediately follow ISE 4970 . Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE student; ISE 3810 , ISE 4310 , and ISE 4970

title: Undergraduate Research in Industrial Engineering
description: Independent investigation or project in industrial engineering. May be repeated to 6 hours.

title: Undergraduate Research Industrial Engineering - Honors
description: Independent investigation or project in industrial engineering. May be repeated to 6 hours. Enrollment limited to receiving departmental honors  Prerequisites: Restricted to IMSE students only

description: Current and new technical developments in industrial engineering. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Engineering Statistics
description: (cross-leveled with IMSE 4110). Understanding and application of statistical analysis of techniques.  Emphasis on hypothesis testing, regression analysis, analysis of variance (ANOVA) and design of experiments (DOE). Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: grade of C- or better in ISE 3110

subject: ISE
title: Deterministic Models in Operations Research
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 4210 ). Study of linear, network, and integer optimization models for deterministic decision-making with emphasis on model development, interpretation, and applications in engineering and management systems. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 2210

subject: ISE
title: Optimization Modeling and Computational Methods
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 4220 ). Modeling and solution techniques for mathematical optimization, including linear, nonlinear, integer, and stochastic programming. Emphasis on formulation of models for most-efficient use of solution algorithms.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 3110 , ISE 4210

subject: ISE
title: Stochastic Models in Operations Research
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 4230 ). Introduces stochastic models and probabilistic optimization for decision-making under uncertainty, emphasizing model formulation, performance analysis, and applications in engineering and management systems. Topics include dynamic programming, Markov chains, Poisson processes, queueing theory, and inventory theory. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Grade of C- or better in ISE 2110 and ISE 3110

subject: ISE
title: Discrete-Event Simulation for Digital Twin Applications
description: (cross-leveled with ISE 4280 ). Introduces principles and methods for modeling and analyzing discrete-event stochastic systems. Lecture topics include queuing theory, Monte Carlo simulation, random number and variate generation, input and output analysis, variance reduction, and simulation-based experiment design. The laboratory component emphasizes developing virtual 3D simulation models using advanced software platforms to represent, analyze, and improve system performance in support of digital twin applications across manufacturing, logistics, and service operations. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Grade of C- or better in ISE 4110

Students will learn cognitive information processing, mental workload, human reliability, decision-making, and empirical methods in HCI research. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Advanced Topics in Industrial & Systems Engineering
description: Current and new technical developments in industrial engineering. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Advanced Manufacturing and Supply Systems
description: The design, regulation, and optimization of manufacturing and supply systems through systems analysis. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Problems in Industrial and Systems Engineering
description: Supervised investigation in industrial engineering to be presented in the form of an engineering report. Graded on A-F basis only.

subject: ISE
title: Industrial Engineering Graduate Seminar
description: Selected topics in industrial engineering; oral presentations and engineering reports. Graded on S/U basis only. Credit Hour s : 0

subject: ISE
title: Design and Analysis of Engineering Experiments
description: Application of advanced statistical methods for the design and analysis of experiments, including two-level factorial designs and fractional factorial designs, response surface methods, and random effects models.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: ISE 4110 or ISE 7110 or equivalent

subject: ISE
title: Linear and Network Optimization
description: Applications of discrete operations research methods, including linear programming, network models, fuzzy sets, integer programming, and meta-heuristics.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Nonlinear Optimization
description: Introduces computational non-linear mathematical programming procedures their use in solving complex industrial systems design problems.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Stochastic Processes and Models
description: Theory and applications of stochastic processes; includes continuous time Markov chain, Markov decision process, queueing theory, and stochastic manufacturing systems.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Advanced Integrated Production Systems
description: Advanced study of the design and operation of flow shop, job shop, and cell-based production systems, including scheduling, layout and material flow issues. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Supply Chain Modeling and Analysis
description: Theory and application of supply chain networks, integration of production and inventory control methods.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Machine Learning and Prescriptive Analytics for Decision Intelligence
description: Explores advanced data analytics, machine learning, and prescriptive analytics methods applied to solving real-world engineering and operations challenges. The course integrates the three pillars of analytics: (i) descriptive analytics for data exploration and visualization, (ii) predictive analytics using supervised and unsupervised learning for prediction, classification, and pattern discovery, and (iii) prescriptive analytics methods that address real-world decision problems through metaheuristic search algorithms and reinforcement learning. Emphasizes Python-based implementation, including data preprocessing, model development, evaluation, and visualization to support intelligent, analytics-driven decisions in manufacturing, supply chain, logistics, healthcare, and service operations. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Advanced CAD/CAM
description: Covers the state-of-the-art in CAD/CAM and explores the latest developments, residual problems, and new direction in CAD/CAM. Includes sculptured surface modeling, rapid prototyping and manufacturing, integrated process planning, shape analysis, machine intelligence.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Advanced Manufacturing Technologies
description: The fundamental theory, design, fabrication, and analysis of state-of-the-art manufacturing technologies will be covered in this course. The course will emphasize production design, CAD/CAM, material selection, and material processing technologies, including traditional machining methods, rapid prototyping and manufacturing, integrated process planning, shape analysis, and cutting-edge Micro/Nanofabrication techniques. The course uses active learning with hands-on projects, videos, and class discussions to help students understand manufacturing principles and product realization methods. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Advanced Reliability Theory
description: Development and application of quantitative models for planning and evaluation of the performance of engineering systems. Prerequisites: ISE 4650 or ISE 7560 Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Strategic Enterprise Management
description: Topics including enterprise strategies, process and content models, strategy implementation, value chain analysis, business processes, systems engineering approaches, business process reengineering, and dynamic systems modeling. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Human Factors
description: Human factors inputs, outputs and environment and their influence on design and evaluation of man and machine systems. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: ISE
title: Research-Masters Thesis in Industrial Engineering
description: Independent investigation in field of industrial engineering to be presented as a thesis. Graded on S/U basis only.

subject: ISE
title: Research-Doctoral Dissertation in Industrial Engineering
description: Independent investigation in field of industrial engineering to be presented as a dissertation. Graded on S/U basis only.

subject: IS_LT
title: Information Management and the Successful Scholar
description: This course will help students determine what information is needed for a project; access and critically evaluate information in the library and the internet; understand intellectual property, develop skills for lifelong learning, and learn to use a variety of technological tools that can help them succeed in college. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Inquiry into Transforming Learning with Technology
description: Students will examine the role of digital technologies in fostering active, equitable, and student-centered learning. This course establishes a foundation for future technology integration coursework by introducing tech integration standards, key concepts, and emerging trends in educational technology. Graded on A-F basis only.  Prerequisites: Instructor's consent required. (Students must be admitted to College of Education & Human Development's Teacher Education program)

subject: IS_LT
title: Blended Learning in the K12 Classroom
description: Introduces the principles and best practices of blending online and in-person instruction to create engaging, student-centered learning experiences in K12 classrooms. Students will explore models of blended learning, digital tools for facilitating blended learning, and strategies for supporting learners and balancing face-to-face and online interactions. Graded on A-F basis only.  Prerequisites: Students must be admitted to College of Education's Teacher Education program and have taken IS_LT 2300 . Instructor's consent required

subject: IS_LT
title: Technologies for Game-Inspired Teaching and Learning
description: Explores how digital tools and game-based strategies can enhance learning outcomes in K-12 classrooms. Pre-service teachers will examine the principles of gamification and game-based learning while evaluating technologies that support motivational, interactive learning experiences. Graded on A-F basis only.  Prerequisites: Students must be admitted to College of Education's Teacher Education program and have taken IS_LT 2300 . Instructor's consent required

subject: IS_LT
title: Advancing Equity in K12 Classrooms Through Artificial Intelligence
description: This course examines how AI-driven strategies can promote equitable and inclusive teaching and learning in K-12 education. Pre-service teachers will explore the potential of AI tools to support diverse student needs and create more flexible, personalized learning experiences. Graded on A-F basis only.  Prerequisites: Instructor's consent required. Students must be admitted to College of Education's Teacher Education program and have taken IS_LT 2300

subject: IS_LT
title: Inquiry into Empowering Learners with Technology
description: This course examines models and strategies for integrating technology into the teaching and learning process, with a focus on transformative, meaningful learning instead of passive technology use.  Topics include digital citizenship, professional online presence, and designing and facilitating learning with technology.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Consent required (students must be admitted to College of Education's Teacher Education program)

subject: IS_LT
title: Introduction to Research in Educational Settings
description: (same as ED_LPA 3450 ). This course provides an introduction to quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods research, with an emphasis on how various forms of data collection and prior research can inform and improve practice. Students will: (1) develop skills in locating research relevant to their professional interests; (2) understand multiple forms of data collection strategies; and (3) identify ethical considerations associated with research. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Making and Education
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7099 ). This course discusses the importance of making and creative, participatory culture in educational environments.  Students will learn about making and participatory creative culture, with an emphasis on inclusive STEAM experiences, while using virtual creative tools. Experience how these ideas can enhance your own personal education, while building practical skills in design thinking and project management. This course includes experience creating digital learning spaces and projects, builds 21st century career skills, and provides a chance to design and prototype educational manipulatives and aids. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 2

subject: IS_LT
title: Computational Thinking
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7201 ). This course introduces computational thinking skills, including inferential (statistical) thinking and algorithmic thinking through instructor-supported computer programming. Key topics include exploratory data analysis, probability and prediction, and statistical tests and modeling, all taught through hands-on data analysis using basic Python programming. Assuming no prior knowledge of statistics or programming, this course is designed as a scaffold to prepare students - especially those from non-STEM backgrounds - for data-related tasks in library and information science, learning technologies, and various other disciplines, including the humanities and social sciences. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Game Engine Skills
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7308 ) This course - via hands-on activities and projects - will immerse you into learning to use the basic functionalities of a Game Engine (e.g. Unity or Unreal). This is a skills course. You will learn to use the game engine so you can prototype games on your own. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 2

subject: IS_LT
title: Seminar in Information Science and Learning Technologies
description: Discussion and critical study of current developments in the field of information science and learning technologies.

subject: IS_LT
title: Principles of Multimedia and Message Design
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7325 ). This course explores fundamental design theory and message design principles essential for effective communication across fields. Students will learn to analyze, critique, and create visually compelling content using design concepts, from typography to color theory, as well as adapt these skills to new and emerging technologies. The course will focus on visual and digital literacy and its importance in design. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 2

subject: IS_LT
title: Writing Educational Objectives
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7326 ). Effective instruction requires precise awareness of what the desired transformation or knowledge gain in learners as a result of the instruction. In this course, students will learn how to clearly articulate objectives for what a learner should achieve or understand by the end of an educational experience. By completing this course, you will gain the skills to write well-defined objectives that serve as the foundation for designing impactful educational experiences. Graded on A-F basis only.

subject: IS_LT
title: Web Design and Development
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7355 ). Learn how to make websites or customize existing ones using HTML5 and CSS3 (cascading style sheets). This course teaches you how to set-up, design and create a website, learn design principles of text, color, media, and how to design web sites for different layouts. You will develop a fully functional website ready to use or one ready for more advanced web languages to be integrated.   Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Interactive Web Design
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7356 ). Attain skills in designing/developing interactive web sites/applications using JavaScript, JavaScript libraries, AJAX, plugins, widgets, Bootstrap, and user interface themes. Add effects, animations to photo galleries, slide shows, carousels to support instruction. Embed dynamic data visualizations using multiple open sources and modify web pages based on user actions to fit interactive instructional needs.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: IS_LT 4355

subject: IS_LT
title: Introduction to Digital Media
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7361 ). Hands-on approach to multimedia production techniques. Develops understanding of technical and conceptual tools for the basics of digital media, video editing, still image and audio file manipulation. Students create web portfolio to present their digital products. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Technology Leadership
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7366 ). Develop skills, knowledge, and values needed to provide technology leadership in diverse environments. Analyze characteristics of effective leaders, with a focus on staff development, project management, and leading innovation. Explore technology integration, policy planning and reform, and current issues across various settings, including schools, libraries, community organizations, and online platforms. Graded on A-F basis. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Exploring Moodle
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7373 ).  This course will prepare students to work within the Moodle Learning Management System (LMS) to set up and manage an online course. Students in the course will investigate and manipulate components of Moodle from an instructor's perspective. Graded on A-F basis only.

subject: IS_LT
title: Exploring Canvas
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7374 ). This course will prepare students to work within the Canvas Learning Management System (LMS) to set up and manage an online course. Students will investigate and manipulate components of Canvas from an instructor's perspective. Graded on A-F basis only.

subject: IS_LT
title: Mobile Learning and Application Design
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7375 ). Mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets have exploded in popularity over the past decade. Students are using their mobile devices to access learning materials at an ever-increasing rate. This course embraces the mobile revolution and provides a perspective of learning that is available 24/7 and from anywhere in the world. To this end, the course provides a brief history of mobile learning (mLearning), an overview of mobile learning hardware, and a specific focus on the software (known as apps) that is used on mobile hardware. Learners identify learning needs, review apps based on those needs, and evaluate those apps. Learners then design and develop functional prototypes of mobile learning apps with user-friendly app development tools. Graded on A-F basis only.  Recommended: Students must be able to hand code: html, Styling and positioning web pages using CSS & JavaScript, and JavaScript basic functions. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Rapid Prototyping for Learning and Information Systems
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7383 ). Students will apply UX design principles and use rapid prototyping tools to create a prototype of an web-based application to support a learning or information seeking need. Specific competencies include: Compare and contrast features of rapid prototyping software tools; Develop a user journey map and functional requirements; Apply UI/UX principles and use prototyping software to develop low-fidelity and high-fidelity prototypes of a web app; Create testing plans, collect data, and iterate prototypes. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Designing Games for Learning
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7384 ). Learn why games can be useful in learning and how to design them. Play some exemplary games that will help you understand the mechanics of game design and work incrementally towards designing and developing your own educational game prototype via game modifications ("mods"), engaging in gaming communities, evaluating existing games, building learning plans using games and learning the basics of a simple gaming shell language. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites or Corequisites: IS_LT 4310 must be taken as a prerequisite or concurrently with IS_LT 4384 Prerequisites: Junior or senior standing required

subject: IS_LT
title: Designing Games for Learning II
description: Learn to apply knowledge of serious game design to a real-world problem within the learning community. Acknowledge and identify the differences in educational games and simulations by playing and researching actual educational games and simulations. Work with a real client to incrementally design either a game or simulation with a working prototype to pitch to Adroit Studios gaming lab. Gain experience with gaming and simulation engines and understand how game development aligns with game design. Test the designed prototype idea to evaluate the success of learning. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: IS_LT 4384 , instructor's consent

subject: IS_LT
title: Microlearning
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7386 ). Microlearning involves just-in-time delivery of small, targeted "nuggets" of specific content. This course introduces basic concepts, process, strategies, and resources for designing microlearning experiences. Students utilize step-by-step guides and instruction to create a microlearning project. Graded on A-F basis only.

subject: IS_LT
title: Techno-literacies: Navigating Information, Data, and AI
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7390 ). In today's complex and evolving information landscape, learners must be equipped with a broad set of literacies to navigate, evaluate, and create knowledge using emerging technologies. This course explores multiliteracies, including information, digital, data, and AI literacy, and their role in learning environments. Through critical inquiry and hands-on practice, students will examine learning technologies and design instructional materials that promote equitable, inclusive, and ethical engagement with information. The course emphasizes AI prompt engineering as a strategic skill for learners and educators in the age of generative AI. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 2

subject: IS_LT
title: Accessible Learning and Information Environments
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7470 ). This course provides an in-depth exploration of accessibility in educational and information environments, with a focus on creating inclusive and accessible learning experiences. Students will develop a foundational understanding of accessibility laws and policies and will apply the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) standards to select, create, and test accessible digital content. The course will emphasize the Universal Design for Learning (UDL) framework and the importance of building an equitable learning environment for all rather than accommodating specific users. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 2

subject: IS_LT
title: Introduction to Project Management
description: Knowledge and tools for major phases of project management life cycle: project initiation, planning, execution, and closure. Integrated online discussions focus on application and resources. Includes discussions of Lean Project Management techniques and the role of Project Managers. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Educational Studies Game Design Senior Capstone
description: In this course students design and prototype a simple educational game or simulation, or a significant component of a larger educational game or simulation design. Once developed, you must conduct play-tests. The capstone is used as the culminating assessment at the end of the program of study. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Instructor's consent required. Must be taken during last semester of student's program

subject: IS_LT
title: Educational Studies Game Design Senior Capstone
description: In this course students design and prototype a simple educational game or simulation, or a significant component of a larger educational game or simulation design. Once developed, you must conduct play-tests. This writing intensive capstone is used as the culminating assessment at the end of the program of study. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: Instructor's consent required. Must be taken during last semester of student's program

subject: IS_LT
title: Intro to VR-enabled Instructional Design
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 7888 ). This course concentrates on establishing your own virtual reality instructional environment applying instructional design theories and hands-on technical skills including 3D modeling and simple scripting in VR. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Making and Education
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 4099 ). This course discusses the importance of making and creative, participatory culture in educational environments.  Students will learn about making and participatory creative culture, with an emphasis on inclusive STEAM experiences, while using virtual creative tools. Experience how these ideas can enhance your own personal education, while building practical skills in design thinking and project management. This course includes experience creating digital learning spaces and projects, builds 21st century career skills, and provides a chance to design and prototype educational manipulatives and aids.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 2

subject: IS_LT
title: Computational Thinking
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 4201 ). This course introduces computational thinking skills, including inferential (statistical) thinking and algorithmic thinking through instructor-supported computer programming. Key topics include exploratory data analysis, probability and prediction, and statistical tests and modeling, all taught through hands-on data analysis using basic Python programming. Assuming no prior knowledge of statistics or programming, this course is designed as a scaffold to prepare students - especially those from non-STEM backgrounds - for data-related tasks in library and information science, learning technologies, and various other disciplines, including the humanities and social sciences. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Library and Information Technology
description: The nature of library and information technologies in the institutional setting; covers the culture of information in society, standards for information processing and transfer, and networking in communications perspectives of information-providing agencies such as libraries and archives.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Organization of Information
description: In order to retrieve and use information, that information must first be organized. This course investigates systems and structures for organizing information in a variety of contexts. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Foundations of Library and Information Science
description: An introduction to the background, contexts, organizations, issues, ethics, values, and terms of information science, the information professions, and the library as an idea, space, institution, and repository of the cultural record. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: School Library Early Field Experience
description: 30-50 clock hours of early field experience in K-12 school libraries. Students will observe an experienced school librarian and have limited interactions with students. Emphasis to include professional library skills in program management and administration (e.g., managing collections and technology) and working with the school community.  Graded on S/U basis only.  Prerequisites: Instructor permission and enrollment in the school library media specialist emphasis area

subject: IS_LT
title: School Library Mid-Level Field Experience
description: 45-60 clock hours of mid-level field experience in K-12 school libraries. Students will observe an experienced school librarian and have structured interactions with students. Emphasis to include professional library skills in information and knowledge (e.g., preparing and leading instruction, classroom management) and teaching for learning (e.g., collaborating with the school community).  Graded on S/U basis only.  Prerequisites: Instructor permission and enrollment in the school library media specialist emphasis area. Enrollment in or successful completion of IS_LT 7306

subject: IS_LT
title: Game Engine Skills
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 4308 ). This course - via hands-on activities and projects - will immerse you into learning to use the basic functionalities of a Game Engine (e.g. Unity or Unreal). This is a skills course. You will learn to use the game engine so you can prototype games on your own. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 2

subject: IS_LT
title: Seminar in Information Science and Learning Technology
description: Discussion and critical study of current developments in the field of information science and learning technologies.

subject: IS_LT
title: Principles of Cataloging and Classification
description: Theory and practice of cataloging and classification of library materials using current standards and tools.  Principles, developments, and trends in cataloging and access to library data. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: IS_LT 7305

subject: IS_LT
title: Collection and Access Management
description: Selection of materials for libraries and information agencies, policies for collection management, freedom and diversity of information, access to information and evaluation of collections and access. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Reference Sources and Services
description: Principles, developments and trends in reference services, reference service organization, and general and specialized print and online sources. Overview of information needs and searching.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Management of Information Agencies
description: Concepts of management applied to libraries and information systems; management tools, programming, models and simulation in an environment of an information producing or disseminating agency. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Emerging Technologies in Libraries
description: Critically examines web technologies, devices, and methods used to access collections and services, promote social interaction, and facilitate communication. Focuses on new and emerging software, resources, and communication methods including their discovery and implementation. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Digital Modeling for Serious Games
description: Through a series of hands-on activities and projects, this course will provide you with the skills and confidence to start creating environments and objects using Blender or a similar modeling program. You will learn to use this modeling program with the intention of using your models for a video game project. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Technology in Schools and Learning Technology Portfolio Development
description: This course supports students in the Technology in Schools emphasis area, and the Learning Technologies and Design masters to develop portfolios to document their achievements of the competencies for their programs. TiS students will demonstrate mastery of the ISTE Standards and commitment to ongoing learning. For Learning Technologies and Design students, they will develop portfolios that demonstrate attainment of the degree competencies documented on the SISLT web site. Web development skills are required.  Graded on A-F basis only.  Prerequisites: Restricted to students admitted into the Technology in Schools emphasis, and students in the Learning Technologies and Design program  who have completed 21 hours in their programs

subject: IS_LT
title: School Library Practicum
description: Directed, project-based experience in school libraries. Graded on S/U basis only.  Prerequisites: admission to MA, initial certification or 24 completed LIS credit hours taken at MU; instructor's consent

subject: IS_LT
title: Practicum in Information Agencies
description: Provides a supervised work experience for master's degree students in a public, academic, or special library. Graded on S/U basis only.  Prerequisites: IS_LT 7301 , IS_LT 7302 or IS_LT 7312 , IS_LT 7314 , IS_LT 7315

subject: IS_LT
title: Rapid Development Tools for Online Learning
description: (cross-leveled with IS_LT 4383 ). Students will apply principles of rapid development and use rapid development tools to create a prototype of an e-learning module that uses technology features that can enhance learning (e.g. learner interactions). Specific competencies include: Storyboard and "rapidly" develop an e-learning module using software designed to support this process; Use software tools that develop specific elements of e-learning (e.g. video, animation, gaming), and incorporate those elements into an e-learning module; Evaluate rapidly developed e-learning products; Compare and contrast features of rapid development software packages. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Python for Information Science
description: Designed to introduce programming and general open source computing concepts using Python. This is a standalone course and assumes no prior knowledge of programming. For those aiming to work in a technical environment, or desiring to work in a technically-adjacent role, knowledge of programming and programming skills are valuable as they bolster student understanding of information systems and help develop problem solving skills. Knowledge of programming can be applied to multiple areas of coursework, including: Analysis of data and information, Developing ways to measure information phenomena, Mining data from sources in various formats for analysis, Applied research of user behavior, Data cleaning and organization for analysis, and Process automation. Good programming skills boost work productivity, and are useful to individual programs of study beyond the initial course, as well as throughout students' professional lives. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Users at the Center: Exploring Information Needs and Behaviors
description: Focuses on theories and research related to information needs and behavior to help students understand the concepts of information, information needs, information search/seeking, and information behavior. With an emphasis on users and their needs, this course prepares students to understand information problems and provides opportunities to discuss how to assist users. Students will gain an understanding of classical theories of information needs and behavior, lead weekly seminar discussions, and collaborate with group member(s) to understand information users' perspectives within the library and information science domain. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Recommended: IS_LT 7314

subject: IS_LT
title: Why We Read, Watch, and Play: Popular Culture Reference and Resources
description: We learn about media information users' needs and ways to support their needs, focusing on popular culture sources such as video games, anime, and comic books. Students can expect to understand the information needs and motivations of media users, as well as appropriate online resources to find diverse media information for users. We will also evaluate currently available online search and recommendation systems for popular culture sources and discuss their strengths and weaknesses and how to improve users' information experiences. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Recommended: IS_LT 7314

subject: IS_LT
title: Public Library Community Partnerships
description: Students will respond to community needs through grant-writing, documentation, and budgeting for partnerships. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Public Library Administration
description: This class is covers three main components: planning, human resources, and budgeting, focusing on public libraries. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: IS_LT 7305 Recommended: IS_LT 9444

subject: IS_LT
title: Budgeting in Libraries
description: Budgeting in Libraries covers topics including basic budgeting principles, the legal context, sources of income, standards, developing budgets, types of budgets, fund accounting, cost concepts, risk, internal controls and budget presentation. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Problems in Information Science and Learning Technology
description: Independent, directed study on a topic in the areas of information science and learning technologies.  Prerequisites: departmental consent

subject: IS_LT
title: Dissertation Research in Information Science and Learning Technologies
description: Dissertation research. Graded on S/U basis only.  Prerequisites: Doctoral Committee Chair's consent

subject: IS_LT
title: Library Information Systems
description: Focuses on the automated library systems marketplace. Covers integrated online library systems from the systems, functional and user perspective. Includes management approaches for procurement and operation of such systems. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: IS_LT 7302 or IS_LT 7312 , and IS_LT 7301 or IS_LT 7320

subject: IS_LT
title: Gender Construction in Children's/Adolescent Literature and Media
description: This course will cover some of the theoretical concepts about the construction of gender in our culture and how that construction is enabled by literature and media for children and adolescents.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: School Library Administration
description: Emphasizes school library administration: program development, implementation, evaluation; planning cycle; budget process; services for diverse school constituencies. Effects of national, state, district guidelines, standards and policies on library media programs. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Sociocultural Aspects of Literacy
description: This course will cover sociocultural and social constructionist theory as they relate to literacy. Sociocultural theory, in terms of literacy, looks at how both social elements and cultural elements interact to impact literacy behaviors and outcomes. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Curriculum and the School Library
description: Focuses on the library media specialist as teacher and instructional partner. Emphasizes negotiating instructional partnerships, integrating information problem-solving models into the curriculum, curriculum mapping, and resource-based learning models. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Intellectual Freedom and Its Discontents
description: The course examines principles and contradictions of intellectual freedom and their relation to librarianship. The nature of free speech, the First Amendment, sources of censorship, and professional disputes about intellectual freedom practice in libraries will be important topics. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Information Policy
description: Examination of the roles of private and public sectors in information policy formation. Includes consideration of social, economic, political and technological issues. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Seminar in Digital Libraries
description: This course is a project-based learning environment that combines Instructor-prepared content, group-based student projects, and threaded asynchronous discussions on selected topics relating to the design, development, and implementation of practical digital libraries. Research directives within the broad domain of digital library development are also covered.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: IS_LT 7301 , IS_LT 7305 , IS_LT 7302 / IS_LT 7312

subject: IS_LT
title: Seminar in Information Science and Learning Technology
description: Discussion and critical study of current developments in information science and learning technologies.

subject: IS_LT
title: Doctoral Seminar in Information Science and Learning Technologies
description: Discussion and critical study of current developments in information science and learning technologies. Graded on A-F basis only.

subject: IS_LT
title: Electronic Resource Management
description: This course explores electronic resources (primarily subscription journals and databases) in terms of products, pricing, in-house management of resources, both technical and organizational, licensing, configuring databases and organizing websites for the end user, statistical reporting, and future trends. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Health and Medical Information and Services in Libraries
description: This class explores health information, services, and programs in all types of libraries and covers trending and relevant topics in the health and medical fields using articles, recordings, and other resources and hands-on assignments to demonstrate how health and medical information plays a role in librarianship.  Graded on A/F basis only Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Action Research
description: Study of concepts associated with action research; and the processes and procedures for conducting action research.  Culminating project is the development of an action research project. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: 12 credit hours completed prior to enrolling

subject: IS_LT
title: American Library History
description: Students in this course will learn about the history of libraries in America, reading about and analyzing the political, cultural, and social roles of particular libraries and the library as in institution. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Scholarly Communication
description: Exploration of the production and communication of information and knowledge in the disciplines. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Usability of Information Systems and Services
description: Introduction to concepts and methods of usability testing and research and user-centered design strategy. Course takes a process approach to define target audiences and usability problems, create and administer investigative procedures, analyze results, and report findings effectively. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Ethics, Data, and Information
description: Critical inquiry into perennial and emerging issues in the ethics of data and information.

subject: IS_LT
title: Diversity in the Information Professions
description: Leadership to promote employment, organizational, collection and program diversity within libraries and information agencies in the U.S. This course includes management and diversity theories, discussions of workplace climate, and discussions of discrimination and hostility issues. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: The Information Society
description: This class critically examines the control, dissemination, and effects of information on the modern world. We will study the complex relationship between information and society, looking at how each is a reflection and shaper of the other. The relationship of libraries and other information agencies to the state, and the role of information professionals in the political and cultural spheres are central themes in the course.   Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: History of Books and Media
description: Examines the history and philosophy of books and media from the beginnings of writing to the Internet, emphasizing the effects of changes in communication and information technologies. The focus is on the social, cultural, intellectual, scientific, and religious impacts of shifts in the media for preserving and transmitting information. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Metadata
description: The contacts in your phone, the embedded GPS information in the photo you took on vacation, and the information that allows you to track down an article in a database are all metadata.  Today more than ever, metadata is at the heart of what information professionals do as we organize, teach about, search for, and analyze information.  This class explores a variety of kinds of metadata, and the tools and systems for working with it, from the point of view of the information professional.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3 Prerequisites: IS_LT 7302 or IS_LT 7312

subject: IS_LT
title: Children's Library Materials
description: Evaluation and selection of materials for children birth-age 13 (Grade 6).  Early literacy, emergent readers, reader response theory; social, cultural contexts of readers and reading, trends in publishing. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Youth Services in Libraries
description: Examines physical, mental, and emotional development of youth birth through high school.  Emphasis on community analysis, outreach services, program design and techniques.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Teen Library Materials
description: Evaluation, selection of print, alternate formats for teens, 13-18 (Grades 7-12).  Personal, social, popular culture contexts of teen readers and texts; emphasizes reader response; challenges common assumptions about teens and reading. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Adult Services in Libraries
description: Library services to adults, including special populations. Emphasis on information needs of adults, organization and management of adult services. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Legal Bibliography and Reference
description: This course provides a broad introduction to the methods and resources for conducting legal research, the collection needs for a law collection, and the needs of legal reference patrons. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Reader Advisory Services
description: Examination of value and role of leisure reading and leisure reading materials.  Coverage of reader advisory techniques, support processes, and resources for providing reader advisory services to various audiences.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Marketing and Libraries
description: This course provides an introduction to marketing - concepts, planning, strategies and evaluation - as related to libraries and information agencies. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Digital Humanities and Information
description: This course on history, philosophy, and methods in the emerging field of 'digital humanities' focuses on topics at the nexus of information, the humanities disciplines, technology, and culture, as well as the contexts of the academy, libraries/archives, museums, and media. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: The Academic Library
description: Development, objectives, organization and structure, nature of the collections and responsibility for their development, philosophy of library services, measurement and standards of library effectiveness. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: The Public Library
description: An overview of public library history, missions, and societal roles.  Includes public library funding, organization, and management. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Special Libraries and Information Centers
description: Introduction to the organization, management, collections, services, challenges and terminology of special libraries and information  centers. Addresses the goals and competencies of special librarianship including information provision and functions as performed in special information centers. Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: International and Comparative Librarianship
description: International libraries, intercultural information concerns, how information agencies differ between nations and global information issues. Course presents various countries, their information infrastructures and the influence of information and communication technologies. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: Human Centered Design
description: Provides an overview of iterative design and project management methodologies that develop solutions to interactive systems and tools.  Students will learn how to implement rapid prototyping and evaluation techniques by focusing on the user and task needs, along with human factors.  The methods and techniques in this course will enhance understanding of task performance, user satisfaction, and design research.  Graded on A-F basis only. Credit Hour s : 3

subject: IS_LT
title: International Libraries in Context
description: Study Abroad course. Visit and study international libraries and related institutions. Covers the political, cultural, social, and economic context in which they operate. Credit Hour s : 3
